title: Aurora POC privacy & ops: benchmark onboarding
summary: Kickoff for POC focused on privacy-first benchmarking and operational constraints. Agreed success criteria (latency, cost per 1k requests, false-positive rate for redaction), outlined workload shape, data handling options (redaction vs no-logging vs encrypted prompts), and plan for two benchmarks: 1) internal synthetic load, 2) production trace replay. Action items: share security pack, run baseline bench, confirm sample dataset and PII examples.
next_steps: Alex to send Redwood security pack and SOC2 artifacts (link) - by 2025-10-09
Aurora to provide 3 days of anonymized production traces or a synthetic workload spec - by 2025-10-14
Meera to schedule baseline benchmark run and share config/benchmark script - target week of 2025-10-20
Follow-up sync to review benchmark results and redaction accuracy - scheduled 2025-10-27 tentative
action_items: Alex Rivera - send security pack + POC checklist (link to deck) - due 2025-10-09
Priya Nair - share sample PII patterns and retention policy doc - due 2025-10-14
Jordan Lee - provide production traces or workload spec (S3 link) - due 2025-10-14
Meera Patel - run baseline latency/cost benchmark and upload logs - due 2025-10-22
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-07 16:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Meera (Redwood SE), Jordan (Aurora Eng Lead), Priya (Aurora Security), Sam (Aurora PM)
Recorded to: fireflies.ai
Links shared: Deck: https://redwood.app/decks/aurora-poc.pdf ; Security pack: https://redwood.app/security/aurora-pack.pdf

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm alex from redwood, i'll kick us off. quick roundtable?
[00:10] Jordan: hi, jordan here - engineering lead at aurora, mainly here to scope the performance side and make sure the POC maps to production traffic.
[00:18] Priya: priya, security and compliance. i'll own redaction/retention requirements.
[00:24] Sam: sam, product - i'll cover success criteria and business context.
[00:30] Meera: meera, redwood solutions engineer - i'll run the benchmarks and help with config.

[01:05] Alex: objective today is scoping a privacy-first POC: what success looks like, what data you'll provide, and how we benchmark latency/cost and redaction. i expect two benchmark runs: synthetic shape and a trace replay. is that what you had in mind?
[01:18] Sam: yes. key thing: our product has a mix of short prompts and longer clinical summarization requests — maybe roughly 70% short chat requests (~150 tokens) and 30% longer (~1.2k tokens). latency for short requests should be < 150ms tail if possible, cost target TBD.
[01:36] Jordan: also we have KV cache usage in prod, large context windows sometimes, so need to see memory profile.
[01:44] Meera: got it - we'll capture sequence length distribution. quick q: are you pro-redaction (we strip PII client-side) or do you want server-side redaction/logging off?
[01:58] Priya: security preference is to minimize PHI leaving our VPC. we prefer client-side redaction but need to validate redaction accuracy for edge cases. if client-side is not practical we'll consider server-side no-logs or immediate redaction with K M S encrypted prompt storage.
[02:18] Alex: noted. so we have three modes to evaluate: a) client-side redaction pre-send, b) server-side automatic redaction + no retention, c) encrypted prompt storage with K M S and audit logs. we'll bench all three for perf and accuracy.

[03:05] Sam: success criteria from product side: 1) latency SLO for short requests (p95), 2) cost per 1k tokens under a threshold, 3) redaction false negative rate < 0.1% on our sample PII set, 4) no privacy incidents in the POC window.
[03:24] Priya: add SOC 2 and SAML/SSO integration as gating items for production, not blocking the POC but must see artifacts.
[03:33] Alex: we'll share SOC2 report and SAML integration guide in the security pack.

[04:10] Jordan: for workload sizing: at peak we expect 120 rps (short requests) and bursts up to 200 rps for a few minutes. average rps is about 30. can you simulate this?
[04:22] Meera: yes, we can run a synthetic load generator to match that burst profile and also replay traces. please confirm whether the sample traces will be anonymized or if you want us to run in your VPC for private trace replay.
[04:38] Priya: we'd prefer to anonymize and avoid raw PHI transfer. we can provide tokenized traces with placeholders for PII categories (NAME, DOB, MRN).
[04:50] Alex: tokenized traces are fine for latency/cost bench; for redaction accuracy we need some raw-ish examples — we can run a redwood agent inside your VPC (private deployment) to test real PII without data leaving your network. that's an option for the later phase.

[06:00] Sam: timeline thoughts? we'd like POC results within 4 weeks: week 1 trace/spec collection, week 2 baseline run, week 3 redaction tests, week 4 results and decision. feasible?
[06:12] Meera: yes that's tight but doable assuming we get traces this week. baseline bench can be automated.
[06:20] Jordan: are there any setup lead times on the redwood side — e.g., dedicated env or VPC peering?
[06:28] Alex: for the hosted baseline nothing special. for private VPC deploy (if you want private replay) we usually run a quick connector and that takes 3-5 working days for networking and K M S integration.

[07:05] Priya: on retention policy - our default requires logs retained no more than 30 days and PII erased within 7 days unless flagged for audit. can redwood enforce per-route retention?
[07:18] Meera: yes, per-route retention is configurable. we can set prompt retention to zero (no storage), or set to 7/30 days and automatic purge. audit logs are separate and can be routed to your SIEM.
[07:32] Priya: audit logs are important; we need immutable audit trails for who accessed what. how do you handle K M S encryption and key ownership?
[07:41] Alex: we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) via major cloud K M S providers. you can own the key and we only store encrypted blobs; audit logs show key use events.

[08:50] Sam: redaction accuracy - what's your redaction engine? do you use heuristics or model-based redaction?
[08:59] Meera: we offer both. lightweight heuristics for names/SSNs and a model-based transformer redactor that learns context. model redaction is higher recall but adds ~30-50ms per request. we'll measure tradeoffs.
[09:15] Jordan: that latency bump could push p95 over the SLO for short requests. can we do hybrid? run model for suspicious cases only?
[09:24] Meera: yes - risk-based hybrid: heuristics first, if ambiguous then model call. reduces avg overhead. we'll include in bench configs.

[10:40] Alex: logging: during POC we can run 'no-logs' mode where we don't persist prompts; instead we stream to ephemeral memory and only keep minimal metadata for billing. that impacts debugging — we do an opt-in debug capture that redacts based on patterns.
[10:58] Priya: good. we also need to test false positives — cases where redaction removes clinically relevant tokens. can we get a report of redaction vs ground truth?
[11:10] Meera: yes, we'll run a redaction evaluation job comparing our redactor output to your ground truth labels and produce precision/recall metrics and example deltas.

[12:30] Jordan: benchmarks - what metrics will you produce? we want p50/p95/p99, tail latencies, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, memory, cost per 1k tokens, redaction precision/recall, and failure rates.
[12:45] Meera: all of the above. we'll also provide per-route cost breakdown and tracer breakdown showing KV cold/hot hit rates (note - transcript may show as K V cache), batching efficiency, and queueing times.

[14:05] Sam: for the trace replay, we will provide three slices: low latency chat, long clinical summs, and mixed bursts. will redwood accept a CSV with request timestamps and payloads?
[14:18] Meera: yes, CSV or newline JSONL with timestamps is fine. if you can't share raw payloads, tokenized placeholders are fine for perf; for redaction we need at least a small golden set with real PII in an air-gapped test or inside your VPC.

[15:30] Priya: we need to confirm retention metadata — can you tag prompts as "sensitive" and have different retention for those?
[15:38] Alex: yes, route-level tags supported. you can mark certain routes as zero-retention or short-retention. we'll document the config.

[16:05] Jordan: security docs — please share S O C 2, pen test summaries, data flow diagrams.
[16:12] Alex: will attach in the security pack link.

[17:00] Sam: what about legal — do we need a DPA or addendum for PII handling during the POC?
[17:08] Alex: standard DPA is available; for POCs we usually run under a simple addendum but we can elevate if you need. legal review may add 1-2 weeks but not required to start baseline perf benches.

[18:25] Meera: technical question about private replay: if we run our redwood agent inside your VPC, we can do end-to-end without prompts leaving your network. you'll need to open egress for our orchestrator or we can run offline — depending on your security posture.
[18:42] Priya: we prefer no egress, so an offline package or on-prem style connector would be best for the redaction golden test. is that supported?
[18:49] Alex: yes, we have a private connector/on-prem package used for regulated customers. setup time ~1 week. we'll include that as an optional path.

[20:00] Jordan: question on model variants: do you fallback to smaller quantized models to save cost and what's impact on redaction?
[20:10] Meera: we'll test a quantized variant for cost bench. redaction model can be co-located; we'll measure quality delta. fallback policies can be configured per-route.

[21:30] Sam: okay recap — our top priorities are accurate redaction (false negative < 0.1%), short-request latency p95 < 150ms, cost under target (we'll define), and no uncontrolled data retention.
[21:46] Alex: agreed. we'll produce an initial POC plan doc and a bench config with scripts.

[22:55] Meera: infra questions — what about K M S key rotation and audit? we support customer key rotation and you get key use audit events.
[23:05] Priya: need to ensure key rotation doesn't break access mid-POC.
[23:12] Alex: we'll coordinate ops; rotation windows can be scheduled. for POC we typically keep keys static unless you prefer rotation testing.

[24:30] Jordan: do you have telemetry on tokenization differences across models? e.g., token counts per clinical note vary and change cost.
[24:40] Meera: yes we'll include tokenizer mapping and token-estimation tool. we'll run a tokenizer pass on your sample traces and provide adjusted cost estimates.

[26:00] Sam: what about RBAC for who can view prompts in the console?
[26:06] Alex: role-based access control supported; you can limit prompt/viewer roles and require approval for debug capture access.

[27:20] Priya: please show me how audit logs look.
[27:25] Meera: we'll push a sample audit export with key events — access, redaction, key usage. expect JSON lines with user, route, action, timestamp.

[29:10] Jordan: any blockers from your side to run the baseline perf?
[29:15] Meera: only waiting on traces or a workload spec. if we get tokenized traces today we can schedule benches in 48 hours.

[31:00] Sam: final decision criteria — we'll evaluate bench data and security artifacts; product stake for buy is if POC meets SLOs and redaction quality is high.
[31:12] Alex: sounds good. i'll send the POC plan and the security pack.

[33:40] Priya: small nit — for compliance reporting we need a CSV of retained events and a purge confirmation. can you provide purge proofs?
[33:50] Meera: yes, we can provide purge tokens and a signed purge log showing object IDs and timestamps.

[35:00] Jordan: also want to run a stress scenario: sudden ramp from 30 rps to 200 rps and see how queues/backpressure behave. include that in bench.
[35:09] Meera: yes will do, we'll include burst profile and observe MAU and queuing.

[37:20] Sam: ok - any other concerns?
[37:25] Priya: just to reiterate: PII patterns doc and retention policy from us, and security pack from you.
[37:32] Alex: understood.

[38:45] Meera: quick note on redaction metrics: we'll deliver a spreadsheet with each example, ground truth labels, redacted output, flags for false pos/neg; this will let you inspect clinically-critical deletions.

[40:00] Alex: let's pick a follow-up date — how about Oct 27 to review bench results?
[40:08] Sam: works for us.

[41:15] Jordan: one more: for the encrypted prompt storage path, what keys are used for HSM?
[41:22] Alex: we support customer-managed HSM/K M S (Cloud HSM or AWS KMS). we store only ciphertext.

[42:30] Priya: on SAML SSO, we need SCIM provisioning; is that in scope?
[42:36] Alex: yes SCIM and SAML supported; we'll include integration docs.

[44:10] Meera: i'll send the initial bench config — it'll include model variant names, batch settings, cache hints, and redaction mode toggles.

[45:20] Sam: thanks, this was productive.
[45:27] Alex: recap next steps and owners — see action items.
[45:35] Priya: will send PII patterns and retention policy by next tuesday.
[45:40] Jordan: we'll try to get anonymized traces by mid-next week.
[45:46] Meera: great, i'll queue the baseline run once i have the traces.

[46:30] Alex: closing — thanks all.
[46:35] (meeting ends)

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-attributions and auto-transcription artifacts (e.g., "K V cache" displayed as spaced letters). Some proper nouns may be transcribed imperfectly.
